narrativeReportMd:
# ResearchDefinition R4 to R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`ResearchDefinition` is a hard breaking removal in the supplied R6 ballot package. R4 has a concrete `ResearchDefinition` resource, while R6 has no same-name StructureDefinition and instead lists `ResearchDefinition` in `fhir-old-types` as an old resource name no longer used in this version.

## Scope
The analysis is scoped to the local `ResearchDefinition` artifact. Inherited base-resource constraints and DomainResource behavior are excluded. R6 `Evidence` and `EvidenceVariable` were checked only because their definitions are the closest local evidence-domain candidates.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 instances with `resourceType: "ResearchDefinition"` will not validate as R6 resources without changing resource identity. The old resource's PICO-style shape--mandatory `population`, optional `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, and `outcome`, all referencing `ResearchElementDefinition`--does not have a lossless same-path R6 counterpart. R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition` and `EvidenceVariable` appear relevant, but they require a semantic remodel rather than a mechanical rename.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issue is `ResearchDefinition:ARTIFACT_IDENTITY:root:5b2a1c`: the R6 artifact is absent. A second material issue, `ResearchDefinition:CONVERSION_OR_MAPPING:pico:0fd3e9`, is that the core question structure and its references require coordinated migration to other evidence resources.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for the mapping decision because the supplied package does not include an official ConceptMap or change note identifying a canonical successor. Implementers should not assume every R4 ResearchDefinition becomes an R6 Evidence instance without reviewing the meaning of its population, exposure, comparator, outcome, library, and metadata fields.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A less disruptive specification path could have retained `ResearchDefinition` as deprecated or provided a formal conversion profile/ConceptMap. The R6 package instead removes the resource identity, which simplifies the current model but shifts conversion responsibility to implementers.

## Follow-up analysis
Coordinate this report with `ResearchElementDefinition`, `Evidence`, and `EvidenceVariable` analyses, and separately assess removed R4 ResearchDefinition search parameters if API compatibility is in scope.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `ResearchDefinition` is not present as an R6 resource. Existing R4 instances, generated model classes, validators, search APIs, and references using `ResearchDefinition` need an explicit migration strategy. The main uncertainty is the official intended replacement, because the supplied inputs identify the type as old but do not provide a ConceptMap.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is not a field-level patch within the same resource. Systems must choose a replacement representation, most plausibly involving R6 `Evidence` and/or `EvidenceVariable`, then remap R4 `population`, `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, `outcome`, and `library` content. This is likely lossy or policy-dependent without an official cross-version map.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the R6 core package does not define `ResearchDefinition`: the assigned file is absent, the R6 package index has no StructureDefinition entry, and `fhir-old-types` lists it as an old resource name. Confidence is medium for replacement guidance because candidate R6 resources were inspected but no authoritative narrative or ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: ResearchDefinition resource is absent from the R6 core package

oldState.summary: R4 defines ResearchDefinition as a concrete draft resource.

semanticText.definition: The ResearchDefinition resource describes the conditional state (population and any exposures being compared within the population) and outcome (if specified) that the knowledge (evidence, assertion, recommendation) is about.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `ResearchDefinition` is a concrete resource specialization of `DomainResource` with local metadata elements and research-question elements.

newState.summary: R6 has no ResearchDefinition StructureDefinition; the name appears only as an old FHIR type.
newState.narrativeMd: In the supplied R6 package, there is no `StructureDefinition-ResearchDefinition.json` and no package-index StructureDefinition record for the canonical URL. The R6 `fhir-old-types` code system includes `ResearchDefinition` among old resource names no longer used.

facts.note: The code system description says these are old resource names no longer used in this version of FHIR.
The removed local content includes canonical metadata, status, subject, library, population, exposure, exposureAlternative, and outcome.

facts.newValue: No valid R6 resourceType with this StructureDefinition

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The same canonical `ResearchDefinition` artifact is absent in R6. The old-types terminology entry confirms this is not a simple missing file in the local package.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation and runtime break. An R4 JSON/XML instance whose `resourceType` is `ResearchDefinition` has no corresponding R6 base resource definition, so strict R6 validators, serializers, generated model classes, REST endpoints, and CapabilityStatement resource declarations cannot treat it as an ordinary R6 resource.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: ResearchDefinition was a draft knowledge-artifact resource and is likely rare in general clinical exchange, but systems that use it for evidence or recommendation semantics can lose machine-interpretable research-question content if migration is skipped.

justification.inferredGoal: Retire or merge a draft evidence-domain resource into the newer R6 evidence model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated R6 ResearchDefinition resource, likely alongside a deprecated ResearchElementDefinition target, for a transition period.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 package gives strong evidence that `ResearchDefinition` was intentionally retired or renamed: no StructureDefinition is present and the name appears in `fhir-old-types`. The inferred goal of retiring a draft R4 evidence-domain resource in favor of the R6 `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable` model is reasonable. The less-breaking option is only partial because preserving old instances would mean keeping the obsolete resource shape, and likely `ResearchElementDefinition`, in base R6, creating parallel ways to represent similar evidence questions and risking indefinite support of the legacy model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base-design alternative would be to keep `ResearchDefinition` as a deprecated R6 resource for one release, with its R4-compatible PICO elements and references either retained or adjusted to deprecated companion resources. That would preserve validation and generated-model compatibility for most R4 data while still allowing guidance to prefer `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable`. The tradeoff is material: R6 would carry duplicate same-domain representations, validators and servers would need to support both, and implementers might continue producing the deprecated resource instead of migrating.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: This would preserve many R4 instances but keep a duplicate legacy evidence-question representation in base R6 and extend support and validation burden.

evidence.quote: An old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR (deleted or renamed).

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows the smallest relevant R4 shape: `status` is mandatory and `population` is mandatory. It is not a valid R6 resource because R6 does not define `ResearchDefinition`.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource identity itself disappeared. This is more severe than a renamed element: R4 data, generated classes, profile differentials, search parameters, REST resource-type switches, and validation pipelines that mention `ResearchDefinition` need a new target model before they can operate against R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `ResearchDefinition` instance becomes R6-invalid at the resource-type level. This affects JSON, XML, RDF, validator schemas, generated POJOs/classes/interfaces, and server metadata. There is no R6 `ResearchDefinition` instance to round-trip back to R4, so the direct R6-to-R4 question is not applicable for same-identity artifacts.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all persisted instances, profiles, references, search parameters, subscriptions, CapabilityStatements, and generated-code references to `ResearchDefinition`. Choose an explicit target representation, likely involving `Evidence` and/or `EvidenceVariable`, then write migration tests that include a minimal instance, an instance with all PICO fields, and instances using canonical `library` logic and metadata.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Because R4 `ResearchDefinition` was draft, a breaking removal may be acceptable for ballot evolution. Still, a backward-compatible deprecation period or bundled ConceptMap would have reduced implementation risk. Without that, each implementation must infer mapping rules from surrounding evidence resources.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `ResearchDefinition` instances have no same-name R6 base resource, so this is a genuine resource-type compatibility break rather than ordinary metadata churn. A strict R6 validator or generated R6 model cannot accept `resourceType: ResearchDefinition` as a normal R6 instance. However, this was FMM 0 trial-use content, public evidence of production dependence appears sparse, and preserving the old resource in base R6 would keep a duplicate legacy evidence-question model beside `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable`. On balance, the break is real but proportionate for this maturity level.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-ResearchDefinition.json defines a concrete draft/trial-use FMM 0 resource with canonical URL http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/ResearchDefinition.
R6 package has no StructureDefinition-ResearchDefinition.json and the R6 package index has no StructureDefinition entry for ResearchDefinition.
R6 CodeSystem-fhir-old-types includes ResearchDefinition as an old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR.

Lightweight checks of MITRE/NIH FHIR-for-research pages, the HL7 Vulcan RWD IG artifacts page, and GitHub code search found examples/generated library support but no clear public production IG that profiles or requires ResearchDefinition.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 FMM 0 and trial-use status substantially soften the stability concern; I did not treat removal alone as enough for Revisit without stronger production-use evidence.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 instance with resourceType ResearchDefinition has no R6 base StructureDefinition, with downstream runtime/API/codegen effects for validators, model classes, REST resource handling, and CapabilityStatements.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have retained deprecated R6 ResearchDefinition and likely ResearchElementDefinition for one transition release. That would preserve many R4 instances, but it would also require R6 servers, validators, search/codegen, and implementers to carry a duplicate legacy evidence-question representation next to the newer Evidence/EvidenceVariable model. A ConceptMap would help migration but would not by itself preserve base instance validity. The base-compatible alternative is therefore only partial and not clearly low-cost.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: the old report is right that this is a hard resource-type break and that any compatible alternative is only partial, but I temper the action judgment because the artifact is FMM 0 and I found no clear public production-use evidence.

findings.title: ResearchDefinition's PICO content model has no lossless same-identity R6 mapping

oldState.summary: R4 ResearchDefinition directly models a research question with mandatory population and optional exposure/comparator/outcome references.
oldState.narrativeMd: The local R4 shape uses `population` `1..1`, `exposure` `0..1`, `exposureAlternative` `0..1`, and `outcome` `0..1`, all as references to `ResearchElementDefinition`. `library` carries formal logic used by the ResearchDefinition.

newState.summary: No R6 ResearchDefinition elements exist; closest candidates remodel variables through Evidence.variableDefinition and EvidenceVariable.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Evidence` defines repeated `variableDefinition` entries with a required `variableRole` code and references to `Group` or `EvidenceVariable`. R6 `EvidenceVariable` defines a variable's meaning. Neither is a same-resource, same-path successor for the R4 ResearchDefinition question container.

facts.note: Likely candidate mapping is an R6 Evidence.variableDefinition with variableRole=population and observed/intended reference.
Candidate mapping needs policy for Evidence.variableDefinition role exposure and observed/intended semantics.
R6 candidate structures have comparator/category concepts but no direct `exposureAlternative` field.
Candidate mapping is likely Evidence.variableDefinition with variableRole=outcome.
R6 Evidence and EvidenceVariable use different relationship and content structures; formal logic references require mapping policy.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The match to R6 `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable` is semantic rather than identity-based. Their root definitions use similar evidence-variable language, but the supplied package has no official cross-version map.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The root removal is the direct hard validation break; this finding captures the migration and round-trip risk after selecting a replacement. A naive transform can preserve resource metadata but still misrepresent whether an old ResearchElementDefinition was a population, exposure, alternative exposure, or outcome, and R6 `Evidence` can contain statistics, certainty, observed/intended variables, and covariates that R4 `ResearchDefinition` cannot represent cleanly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrectly mapping population, comparator, or outcome definitions can change the meaning of evidence or recommendation logic. The risk is domain-specific but material for evidence-based guidance systems.

justification.inferredGoal: Move from the R4 ResearchDefinition/ResearchElementDefinition model to the R6 Evidence/EvidenceVariable model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old PICO content model in a deprecated R6 ResearchDefinition or other base transitional structure; a ConceptMap alone is migration mitigation, not a base-compatible alternative.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R4 structure directly encoded population, exposure, alternative exposure, outcome, and library links, while the R6 evidence model uses `Evidence.variableDefinition` and `EvidenceVariable` with a different and broader representation. Moving to that richer model is a reasonable goal, especially for a draft R4 resource, but the existing report's ConceptMap or extension-pack idea should not be counted as a `Yes` alternative because it is conversion guidance rather than a less-breaking base R6 design. A true base-design alternative exists only by carrying the old PICO shape forward, and that has material interoperability and maintenance costs.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A backward-compatible base design could have retained the old `ResearchDefinition` PICO fields in a deprecated resource, or introduced a transitional base R6 structure accepted by validators for the old roles while steering new content to `Evidence`/`EvidenceVariable`. That would protect many R4-to-R6 migrations, but it would be incomplete for richer R6 `Evidence` content and would create duplicate ways to represent the same research-question facts. An official ConceptMap would still be useful, but by itself it would not make old R4 instances valid in R6 and therefore is not the backward-compatible base alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retaining old fields would preserve common R4 PICO instances but duplicate representations and leave ambiguous canonical R6 modeling; conversion guidance alone would not preserve R4-valid instances.

R4 has a distinct optional alternative exposure element.
R6 Evidence uses repeated variableDefinition entries rather than the R4 ResearchDefinition PICO fields.

evidence.detail: No supplied R6 ConceptMap was found that names ResearchDefinition as a source or target.

certainty.description: R6 certainty assessment not present in R4 ResearchDefinition

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative only. It shows the kind of remodel an implementer may choose, not an official mapping. The R6 example demonstrates why treating R6 Evidence as a reversible ResearchDefinition replacement is unsafe.

findings.narrativeMd: Even after accepting that `ResearchDefinition` is removed, the data model change is not just a resourceType rename. The R4 resource is a compact container for a research question, while the R6 candidates distribute similar concepts across variable definitions and evidence content. The especially sensitive field is `exposureAlternative`, because a comparator can affect interpretation of evidence and recommendations.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: This finding is not an independent same-resource validation failure; the root deletion already causes that. It is a conversion and semantic compatibility risk. R4-to-R6 transforms must choose how to express each PICO role. R6-to-R4 transforms from `Evidence` back to `ResearchDefinition` are likely lossy because R6 can represent covariates, observed versus intended variables, statistics, certainty, and richer variable metadata that the R4 ResearchDefinition shape does not contain.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not perform a blind text substitution from `ResearchDefinition` to `Evidence`. First migrate referenced `ResearchElementDefinition` resources, probably to `EvidenceVariable`, then map each old PICO role intentionally. Preserve old canonical URLs and identifiers where possible, use `relatesTo` or extensions for provenance if needed, and manually review instances with comparator/exposureAlternative semantics or formal `library` logic.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The redesign may be semantically justified, but it would have been less disruptive with an official ConceptMap and explicit extensions for old fields. Without those, different implementers may create incompatible R6 representations for the same R4 ResearchDefinition.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official R6 narrative/migration material before standardizing a production transform. The supplied package identifies the old type but does not name a successor.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The PICO fields are not just renamed into R6. R4 has role-specific links such as mandatory `population`, optional `exposure`, optional `exposureAlternative`, optional `outcome`, and `library`; the closest R6 structures use repeated `Evidence.variableDefinition` entries and separate `EvidenceVariable` resources. That makes migration policy-dependent, especially for comparator/alternative exposure and formal logic references. Still, this conversion risk is downstream of a draft FMM 0 resource removal, and carrying the old PICO shape in base R6 would create parallel representations of the same evidence-question concepts. The migration burden is real, but the redesign appears proportionate.
keyEvidence: R4 ResearchDefinition.population is 1..1 Reference(ResearchElementDefinition); exposure, exposureAlternative, and outcome are 0..1 references to ResearchElementDefinition; library is 0..* canonical(Library).
R4 ResearchElementDefinition defines PICO elements and has required type codes population, exposure, or outcome.

R6 Evidence.variableDefinition is 0..* with required variableRole and observed/intended references to Group or EvidenceVariable; R6 variable-role codes are population, exposure, outcome, and covariate.

The R6 package contains Evidence and EvidenceVariable StructureDefinitions but no ResearchDefinition or ResearchElementDefinition StructureDefinitions, and local search found ResearchDefinition only in fhir-old-types.
No supplied R6 ConceptMap or same-identity successor mapping for ResearchDefinition was found in the package evidence.
freshReview.fmmEffect: FMM 0/trial-use lowers the expectation that R6 must preserve the old PICO wire model; it does not eliminate the need for careful migration, but it makes a breaking remodel more acceptable absent clear production dependence.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: the strongest independent issue is semantic/conversion loss rather than a separate validation break, because mapping between R4 role-specific PICO fields and R6 Evidence/EvidenceVariable variable definitions can require implementation policy and may not round-trip.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A base-compatible option would be to keep the old PICO fields in a deprecated ResearchDefinition or transitional R6 structure while recommending Evidence/EvidenceVariable for new content. That would preserve common R4 mappings but would duplicate the canonical R6 evidence model and introduce precedence/interoperability questions between old role-specific fields and new variableDefinition structures. An official ConceptMap or StructureMap would be valuable migration guidance, but it is mitigation rather than a less-breaking base design.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing impact and alternative judgment: I agree there is high semantic migration risk and no lossless same-identity mapping, but I treat it as a downstream conversion issue softened by FMM 0 rather than an additional hard break demanding redesign.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 `ResearchDefinition` has no local slicing in the inspected StructureDefinition. There is no R6 counterpart where a slicing delta could occur; the artifact removal is reported separately.
No local R4 `ResearchDefinition` elements had fixed, pattern, or default values requiring separate migration analysis.
No local R4 `ResearchDefinition` elements had maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue restrictions beyond datatype-level rules.

The only local R4 constraint identified was `rsd-0` on `name`; base `dom-*`, `ele-1`, and extension constraints are inherited and out of scope. Because R6 has no ResearchDefinition, there is no same-artifact constraint comparison beyond removal.

R4 bindings on `status`, `subject[x]`, `jurisdiction`, and `topic` were reviewed. There are no R6 ResearchDefinition bindings to compare; terminology details only matter after selecting a target resource.
R4 `status` is a local modifier element and inherited `implicitRules`/`modifierExtension` are base-scope. With no R6 ResearchDefinition, modifier flag comparison is subsumed by the resource removal.
R4 summary flags were reviewed for local elements. The summary surface disappears with the resource and must be reconsidered in the chosen R6 target resource.

No element-level serialization rename was assessed because the R6 artifact is absent. The material serialization break is at `resourceType`/class identity level and is covered by the artifact-identity finding.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 retains ResearchDefinition only as an old-type code
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The old-type terminology entry is not itself a resource definition and does not make R4 instances valid in R6. It is useful evidence and may help tooling produce better diagnostics.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Validators and converters can use this code system to distinguish an intentionally retired/renamed resource type from an unknown typo.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Evidence and EvidenceVariable preserve related evidence-variable concepts
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The existence of candidate resources is not a compatibility break by itself; the break is the removal of `ResearchDefinition`. These resources may reduce migration burden but do not provide a same-identity replacement.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: When designing migrations, compare R4 `ResearchDefinition` together with referenced `ResearchElementDefinition` resources against R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition` and `EvidenceVariable` rather than mapping the resource in isolation.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: `ResearchDefinition.population`, `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, and `outcome` all reference `ResearchElementDefinition`; R6 also lists `ResearchElementDefinition` as an old type. A safe migration must coordinate both resource removals.
R6 `Evidence` is the closest inspected candidate for representing variables, statistics, and certainty related to evidence. Its report should own its own R4-to-R6 changes.
R6 `EvidenceVariable` is a likely migration target for old `ResearchElementDefinition` references used by `ResearchDefinition`.
R4 defines multiple SearchParameters for ResearchDefinition. Since the resource is absent in R6, API search compatibility should be assessed separately if REST behavior is in scope.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The analysis did not include an official R4-to-R6 diff, ballot change request, or committee rationale explaining the removal.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official diff or change note stating the intended successor and rationale would improve justification and migration confidence.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official ConceptMap or conversion script was available for mapping R4 ResearchDefinition instances to R6 Evidence/EvidenceVariable patterns.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A published cross-version ConceptMap or implementation guide with examples for population, exposure, comparator, outcome, and library mappings would resolve most ambiguity.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions were not compared for old R4 bindings because there is no R6 ResearchDefinition binding surface. Terminology may still matter in a chosen target mapping.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansion comparisons after selecting target R6 resources and profiles.
